papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained student models so they retain functionality while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logits-based soft-label supervision to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware mappings, adversarial and contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or heterogeneous-device protocols. Empirical and theoretical work indicates KD often acts both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, task alignment, and careful design of objectives and model interfaces. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data scarcity or domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, principled layer-to-layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating teacher-induced biases.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied set of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teacher ensembles or single models. The literature shows a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (soft logits, feature- and attention-level targets, relational/contrastive objectives), protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, self- or co-distillation), and engineering integrations (projector adapters, curriculum or confidence-weighting, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and cross-modal tasks indicates that carefully designed KD pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and mitigating failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare-output behavior, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and highly practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD techniques range from simple soft-target matching to representation- and task-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of biases and distribution shift. Treated as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline and designed with task constraints in mind, KD yields reliable tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity for deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core set of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, or privacy. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning internal features, attention maps, and layer correspondences; they are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics, and architecture search. KD supports many practical settings — including data-limited, data-free, few-shot, federated, and cross-modal scenarios — but its effectiveness depends on choices such as which teacher signals to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases. Ongoing directions include principled theory for transfer objectives, robust and private distillation, and task-aware designs for structured outputs.

papers_seen.author: Massey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets and training protocols and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently yields large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and explicit mitigations for failure modes such as bias transfer, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift. Important open directions include principled theory linking distillation signals to student generalization, automated teacher–student co-design, and robust, privacy-aware distillation for heterogeneous or data-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are widely used to transfer behavior from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Work across vision, generative modeling, reinforcement learning, recommendation, and language has developed diverse objectives and mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, adversarial synthesis of training data, multi-teacher/ensemble supervision, layer-wise and task-adaptive compression, and data-augmentation-enhanced distillation. These approaches trade off accuracy, inference cost, and robustness and address practical constraints such as lack of access to original training data, domain shift, fairness, and heterogeneous model architectures. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or sometimes match teacher performance while substantially reducing FLOPs, parameters, or latency, but limitations remain in data heterogeneity, low-frequency token transfer, and privacy-constrained settings. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical findings, applications, and open challenges documented in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices, supports domain adaptation and privacy-aware workflows, and integrates naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, objective design, and handling of distributional or architectural mismatch. Real-world deployments therefore require KD to be treated as a configurable component within a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly addresses data availability, robustness, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD encompasses a range of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structures), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation), and deployment strategies (data‑constrained, privacy‑aware, federated and heterogeneous devices). While KD is an effective first‑line tool for many compression needs, its success depends on careful choice of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires explicit safeguards against propagating teacher errors, biased behavior, and degradation on low‑frequency or out‑of‑distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Strategies, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of task performance. The literature shows a broad toolkit—soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and layer-mapping objectives, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and multi-teacher or self-distillation protocols—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical evidence indicates KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve low-precision and deployment behavior, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful alignment of objectives and training procedures. Open problems remain around robustness, distribution shift, low-frequency behavior, fairness, and principled design of teacher–student pairings and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential Tool for Practical Deep Learning — Potentials, Pitfalls, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have matured into indispensable tools for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained, privacy-sensitive, and latency-critical environments. Across modalities—vision, language, speech, and generation—KD enables smaller or heterogeneous models to approach teacher performance, improves interpretability in specific settings, and reduces communication costs in distributed learning. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, suffer under data heterogeneity, and interact subtly with training practices. Careful choices—selective sample usage, multi- or self-distillation, architectural adapters, annealing strategies, and privacy-aware generative replay—help realize KD's benefits while mitigating its limitations. This paper synthesizes evidence from applied and theoretical work to argue that KD should be treated as a central engineering primitive, accompanied by the practices needed for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Evidence, Methods, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically validated set of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A broad toolkit—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware synthesis, and curriculum or adversarial sample selection—enables students to retain much of teacher performance across vision, language, multimodal, retrieval, and federated settings. Despite strong empirical successes, important engineering and scientific challenges remain around teacher–student alignment, data availability and synthesis, preservation of low-frequency behaviors, robustness and fairness, and principled automated design for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade KD variants—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to representation-level matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware protocols—have been adapted to many tasks and modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal, generative models, and federated settings). Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves most teacher performance while enabling large reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count; success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability, and optimization. Remaining challenges include principled theory for when and what to transfer, reliable distillation across heterogeneous architectures and non‑i.i.d. data, mitigation of bias and teacher errors, and robust data-free or privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Costa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD enables substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while recovering much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, speech, recommendation, and multimodal tasks. Effective distillation depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability and handling of data (including data-free and privacy-aware methods), and combination with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Although KD routinely delivers strong empirical gains, persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity gaps, distributional and domain shifts, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, mitigation of transferred biases, and principled automated co-design for hardware-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, task‑aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners match soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures, and even synthesized or privacy-aware pseudo-data to train compact students. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), curriculum and data strategies, and explicit teacher–student alignment; however, important limitations remain in distribution shift, low‑frequency phenomena, heterogeneous architectures, privacy and federated settings, and principled teacher selection. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, practical guidance, and open challenges distilled from the supplied literature.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and sometimes more interpretable students. KD spans logits- and feature-based transfers, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and task-specific adaptations. Its strengths include enabling deployment on resource-constrained hardware, improving latency and memory footprints, and supporting privacy- or data-constrained scenarios. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: teacher quality, data availability and mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, architectural alignment, and deployment heterogeneity require complementary techniques and task-aware engineering to realize reliable, robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature, attention, relational, and data‑free objectives—enable substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success is conditional on task-aware choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression primitives; open challenges remain in capacity mismatch, distributional robustness, preservation of rare behaviors, and privacy-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for transferring predictive behavior from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, efficient students. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods extend beyond logits-matching to include intermediate-feature and attention-level transfer, data-free and privacy-aware variants, multi-teacher and online protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much teacher performance, but success depends on careful selection of what and how to transfer, data availability, and the match between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible, but Not Panacea Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students and for transferring task- or modality-specific capabilities. KD supports many transfer targets and training protocols and can be combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. However, reliable outcomes require careful teacher–student design, attention to data and privacy constraints, and targeted solutions for failure modes such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and preserved low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Haney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Context‑Aware, and Best Used in Hybrid Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Empirical and methodological work shows KD supports a variety of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps) and training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free), and that its benefits are maximized when chosen signals, student capacity, and data strategies are aligned with task and deployment constraints. KD reliably improves student performance but is not always sufficient on its own: the best, robust deployment outcomes arise when KD is integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with safeguards to mitigate transferred biases and data mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, efficient student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade, KD methods have evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and online regimes, and data‑free or adversarial synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance and in many cases improve generalization, but practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of signals to transfer, and the availability and match of distillation data; reliable deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—ranging from soft logits to intermediate-feature and adversarial or data-free methods—has been developed and applied across vision, language, speech, and multimodal problems. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signal to student capacity and data regime, combining KD with other compression methods, and explicitly addressing known failure modes such as teacher bias, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger systems. Across modalities and tasks—including classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and sequence prediction—distillation has been adapted to transfer ensemble knowledge, reduce computation and storage, improve generalization and fairness, enable private or federated deployment, and inject specialized inductive biases. While effective, distillation requires careful design choices (teacher quality, which examples to transfer, whether to use intermediate-layer alignment, robustness and privacy mechanisms) to avoid failure modes. This work argues that KD should be treated not just as a compression trick but as a unifying framework for controlled transfer of behaviors, and outlines empirical and theoretical findings that guide best practices for its application.

papers_seen.author: Simpson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Component of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods vary in their transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training paradigms (offline, online, multi‑teacher, meta‑learned teachers, data‑free synthesis), and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across retrieval, vision, speech, and NLP shows distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but reliable deployment requires task‑aware design choices, careful teacher–student alignment, suitable data strategies (including synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols), and explicit safeguards against propagated teacher artifacts and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD supports a wide range of transfer targets and training regimes and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of risks such as bias transfer and distribution-shift degradation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Collier
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Versatile, but Context-Dependent — A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It reliably transfers useful behavior and internal structure across vision and NLP tasks when designed with task-aware objectives, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data and augmentation choices, student capacity, and complementary compression procedures. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to produce smaller, faster models while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. Approaches vary from matching final logits to transferring internal representations, attention maps, or layer-wise information, and they are applied across modalities including NLP, vision, speech, and reinforcement learning. Practical extensions address multi-teacher setups, data-free scenarios, domain adaptation, quantization, and architecture-aware compression; remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, data heterogeneity, fairness, and reliably preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained devices, and support privacy- or resource-constrained settings. Approaches span soft-label distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, data-free and zero-shot methods, multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, self-distillation, task- and modality-specific objectives, and combinations with pruning. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D detection, recommender systems, and multiple NLP tasks demonstrates that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while significantly reducing latency and memory. The literature also provides growing theoretical insight into when and how distillation helps, and identifies open challenges including imperfect teachers, domain shift, low-frequency token fidelity, modality mismatch, and heterogeneous-device federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Coffey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods span soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or contrastive objectives, and specialized protocols for data-free, federated, cross‑modal, and adversarial settings. KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Costa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD enables substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while recovering much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, speech, recommendation, and multimodal tasks. Effective distillation depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability and handling of data (including data-free and privacy-aware methods), and combination with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Although KD routinely delivers strong empirical gains, persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity gaps, distributional and domain shifts, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, mitigation of transferred biases, and principled automated co-design for hardware-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across modalities and tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when applied with task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints. However, KD is not automatic: its benefits depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and complementary compression methods; it also requires safeguards to avoid propagating teacher errors or biases. When treated as a configurable component of compression pipelines and paired with targeted techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data strategies, and selection of transfer signals), KD is the most practical first-line strategy for many deployment scenarios in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable models while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature shows a wide range of KD mechanisms (logit- and feature-based losses, adversarial and data-free schemes, multi-teacher and online protocols) and application domains (NLP, vision, multimodal, detection, federated settings). KD succeeds best when combined with complementary practices—pretraining, layer-wise alignment, data augmentation, teacher adaptation, and hardware-aware compression—but it faces limitations from teacher errors, data absence, distributional mismatch, and heterogeneous deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes empirical findings, methodological variants, use-cases, limitations, and practical recommendations for knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques in deep learning and NLP. Drawing solely on the provided studies, it highlights common transfer targets and training regimes, domain- and task-specific adaptations, and recurring failure modes, and offers guidance on when and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Core, Conditional, and Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task‑aware component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, or multi-teacher ensembles), KD routinely delivers large reductions in latency and memory while preserving most teacher performance. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy; KD is therefore best used as a first-line, integrated tool rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Dependent Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practically indispensable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count. Its effectiveness depends on deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student design and capacity alignment, data availability and selection, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a standalone recipe, KD delivers the most reliable and deployable gains.

papers_seen.author: Spence
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques that should be treated as an essential, task-aware component of model-compression pipelines rather than a one-size-fits-all solution. Properly designed KD—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, selecting or synthesizing suitable data, and integrating complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—regularly yields compact models that preserve most teacher performance for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. However, KD has predictable failure modes (teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and degradation on rare outputs) that require explicit mitigation and evaluation in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical tool for compressing large models into efficient students, but it must be applied conditionally and integrated with task‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities when teacher quality, student capacity, distilled signals, and data regimes are aligned; however, known failure modes (teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, propagation of teacher artifacts, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena) require targeted remedies and validation for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, KD techniques (logits, feature/attention matching, relational objectives, adversarial and data‑free protocols, and ensemble/online schemes) often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when paired with appropriate data strategies, pretraining, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD has concrete limits — teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, rare‑token degradation, and failures under distribution shift or scarce/private data — which motivate task‑aware design, multi‑signal objectives, and integration with other compression primitives. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, domain examples, practical guidelines, and open challenges documented in the selected literature.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, multimodal tasks and specialized settings (e.g., 3D detection, ranking, medical imaging), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data or synthetic alternatives are used; KD is most effective when used as a configurable component combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware training strategies.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for producing compact models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and complementary compression methods enable substantial reductions in computation, memory, and latency while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to reduce the resource footprint of large neural networks while preserving performance. The literature surveys a range of approaches — from vanilla teacher-student soft-target transfers to layer-wise, attention- and channel-wise methods, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with pruning and adversarial training — and demonstrates successful applications across NLP, speech, vision, graph, and multimodal problems. Empirical results show effective speedups and parameter reductions with modest accuracy loss; theoretical and empirical analyses also connect KD to label-smoothing and regularization effects that can improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically driven framework for transferring predictive and representational information from large or composite teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The literature shows a broad set of distillation objectives (soft logits, intermediate feature matching, attention and relational transfer, contrastive and adversarial schemes), multiple training protocols (multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free and synthetic-data approaches), and tight integration with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance in many settings, enable cross-modal and domain adaptation, and produce dramatic runtime and memory gains when applied with task-aware choices of signals, data, and student architectures. Important failure modes remain—teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, and fairness/privacy concerns—so best practice treats KD as a configurable toolbox that must be tailored to the task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across architectures and modalities, KD methods reduce inference cost and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance; they are adaptable to settings with limited or no original training data and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pretraining-aware workflows. Success in practice depends on careful choice of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data and augmentation strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled theory for diverse distillation objectives, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broadly applicable framework that enables compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teachers to smaller students. KD methods span logits, intermediate-feature and relational matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and cross-modal variants, and complementary integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance and provides regularization benefits, its practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one-shot cure, and addresses robustness, privacy, and distribution-shift concerns through protocol design and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Multifaceted Argument for Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized students that retain much of the teacher's performance. KD has been extended beyond simple logit matching to transfer intermediate representations, channel- or attention-level signals, ranking and relational knowledge, and to operate in data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful training protocols, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and domain constraints; however, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias propagation and degraded modeling of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Sensitive Path for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven and versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around appropriate transfer targets, teacher–student alignment, and data regimes, KD frequently enables substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on task and deployment constraints, and KD must often be combined with complementary methods and task-aware design to avoid failure modes and to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Findings from the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. The literature treats KD as a flexible, configurable component of compression pipelines rather than a single recipe: methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel- or relation-level signals), how transfer is organized (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free/zero-shot), and how KD is combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, adversarial training). Empirical evidence shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the chosen distillation signals and objectives, and data availability or synthesis strategies. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable, task-aware tool integrated with other compression and robustness practices.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central approach for transferring behavior from large, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, more efficient models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD is used both as a compression technique and as a means to inject inductive biases, stabilize continual learning, preserve privacy, and improve efficiency (compute, memory, latency) under deployment constraints. Practical KD pipelines combine logit-based supervision, intermediate-feature matching, architectural replacements, and training-time regularizers; they are often complemented with pruning, low-precision numerics, layer skipping, data augmentation, or specialized alignment strategies to handle mismatched inputs or modalities. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can capture “dark knowledge” beyond labels, transfer inductive biases, and sometimes enable students to outperform their teachers when paired with careful pre-training, data strategies, or architectural design. This synthesis summarizes techniques, motivations, and empirical patterns found in recent studies, and highlights open engineering considerations for applying KD in NLP, vision, graph, and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Practical Model Compression: Evidence, Techniques, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable paradigm for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative models) and use-cases (edge deployment, federated learning, domain adaptation, continual learning), distillation has repeatedly enabled dramatic reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining or even improving task performance. However, distillation is not a panacea: careful design of what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), how to align teacher and student inputs and layers, and when to apply supplementary strategies (adversarial examples, multi-teacher weighting, continual updates) is necessary to avoid failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, misalignment across detectors, and limits in compressing some model families. Drawing on empirical results and method innovations across the literature, I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational component of any deployment-oriented model compression pipeline, and that combining complementary distillation techniques tailored to the task and architecture yields the best balance of compactness, speed, and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and hardware constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and in diverse protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can even improve generalization in some settings, but it also has well-known failure modes—teacher bias propagation, difficulty preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and sensitivity to data availability and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, as well as careful data and objective design.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory and compute while preserving much of task performance. KD techniques span logits/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and contrastive signals, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data-free or domain-adaptive variants. Empirical evidence shows KD is a practical first-line strategy for deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, but it is not a standalone cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, objective design, and careful integration with complementary compression tools. For robust, real-world deployment, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with targeted engineering to mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across domains and tasks—language modeling and translation, recommendation, graph learning, vision, continual and domain adaptation, and resource-constrained deployment—KD enables trade-offs between accuracy, latency, memory, privacy, and train-time complexity. Variants such as feature mimicking, self- and teacher-free distillation, ensemble and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations extend KD’s applicability. At the same time, careful choice of training targets, treatment of low-frequency phenomena, and consideration of the teacher-student mismatch are necessary to avoid transferring teacher errors and to realize the full benefits of distillation.
