papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central tool to transfer performance from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones across modalities and tasks. The field encompasses diverse mechanisms — from soft-target supervision and feature imitation to contrastive and adversarial schemes — and integrates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work highlights when and why different formulations help, how to handle limited or absent teacher data, and which practical choices matter for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific demands.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Efficient and Robust Deep Models: Evidence, Techniques, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher→student transfer recipe into a broad set of methods that enable model compression, robustness, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving training, and architectural search. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, speech, vision, graphs, ranking and recommender systems—KD-based approaches consistently trade minimal performance loss for large gains in speed, memory, interpretability or deployability. The diversity of KD formulations (feature-based, layer-mapping, data-free, online/mutual, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, and task-adaptive compression) provides practitioners with targeted tools to address constraints such as limited data, non-iid federated shards, low-frequency tokens in translation, and privacy requirements. Based on empirical results across the literature, KD should be considered a first-order technique in any pipeline that must deliver high-quality models under resource, privacy, or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach to compress large or ensemble models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, distillation can recover accuracy for lightweight architectures, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and transfer specialized properties (e.g., temporal, structural, or ensemble knowledge). However, distillation is not a panacea: its success depends on the choice of teacher, student architecture and capacity, the training protocol (including data augmentation and sample selection), and implementation details that affect optimization. When these factors are treated carefully, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, architecture design, quantization) and can be adapted to domain-specific needs such as federated learning, retrieval, and vision-language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-Class, Task-Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and useful properties of larger teachers. KD has repeatedly proven effective across modalities and tasks, enabling efficient deployment on constrained hardware, supporting domain and modality transfer, and integrating with complementary compression techniques. However, its benefits are conditional: success depends on teacher quality, data design, augmentation, and careful objective selection, and KD can transfer teacher errors or undesirable biases unless explicitly mitigated. Treating KD as a configurable toolkit—combining logit-level supervision, representation matching, data-side interventions, and deployment-aware protocols—yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance and functionality of larger teacher models. KD is highly versatile—operating at the level of logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and generative models). However, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and the design of distillation objectives; consequently KD should be treated as a configurable component that is combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Carson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods are diverse—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free protocols—and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware data and optimization strategies. Empirical work shows KD routinely delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but important limitations remain around teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, privacy, and reliable preservation of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to produce smaller, faster models while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. Approaches vary from matching final logits to transferring internal representations, attention maps, or layer-wise information, and they are applied across modalities including NLP, vision, speech, and reinforcement learning. Practical extensions address multi-teacher setups, data-free scenarios, domain adaptation, quantization, and architecture-aware compression; remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, data heterogeneity, fairness, and reliably preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Multifaceted Argument for Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized students that retain much of the teacher's performance. KD has been extended beyond simple logit matching to transfer intermediate representations, channel- or attention-level signals, ranking and relational knowledge, and to operate in data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful training protocols, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and domain constraints; however, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias propagation and degraded modeling of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, multimodal and generative settings. KD techniques transfer teacher behavior via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational objectives, and can be extended to data-free, privacy-preserving, and adversarial regimes. Best results arise when distillation is combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search); remaining challenges include data- or domain-limited scenarios, teacher–student mismatch, robustness and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, objective design, and architecture alignment. To realize KD's benefits in production and research, practitioners should treat distillation as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits and representation matching, data-aware schedules or synthesis, and complementary compression methods—while applying targeted safeguards for robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hughes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, and privacy). KD spans logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, many-to-many layer mappings, online and multi‑teacher protocols, and data‑free or synthetic‑data variants. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, distillation signals, data availability, and safeguards against bias and privacy leakage. Thus KD should be treated as a configurable core of compression pipelines—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and task‑aware engineering—rather than a plug‑and‑play cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely used family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods have expanded from simple logits-matching to include feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free and federated protocols, and many-to-many teacher–student mappings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability or synthesis. KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broadly applicable framework that enables compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teachers to smaller students. KD methods span logits, intermediate-feature and relational matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and cross-modal variants, and complementary integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance and provides regularization benefits, its practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one-shot cure, and addresses robustness, privacy, and distribution-shift concerns through protocol design and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applied practical framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), training protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, meta-learned teachers, curriculum-based schedules), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, data-free, privacy-preserving federated protocols) has been developed and adapted across modalities. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large portion of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, choice of distilled signals, and availability or synthesis of training data. Important open problems include handling teacher–student mismatches, preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases, and formalizing best-practice co-designs that combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD spans logits/soft-label matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data‑free and privacy-aware protocols, and self- or teacher-free variants. When combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and task constraints, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. Practical deployment requires task-aware choices, careful alignment of teacher and student, and explicit mitigations for distributional mismatch, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases; important open problems remain in principled theory, robust/private data-free distillation, and heterogeneous architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. The field encompasses a variety of distillation targets (soft logits, internal features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline teacher supervision, online/mutual teaching, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher ensembles), and auxiliary mechanisms (data‑free synthesis, projector layers, many‑to‑many layer mapping). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and graph domains shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and architecture alignment are carefully addressed. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and when designers attend to failure modes including teacher error propagation, degraded rare‑token behavior, distributional mismatch, and fairness or privacy risks. Open directions include principled theory for when particular signals help, robust distillation under data scarcity or heterogeneous deployments, and reliable extensions to generative and structured‑prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. The literature shows that appropriately chosen distillation signals, teacher–student design, and data strategies allow compact models to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and adapt to constraints such as privacy, heterogeneous devices, and limited or unlabeled data. Despite widespread empirical success, important limitations persist—teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, degraded rare-output behavior, and theoretical gaps linking distillation signals to student generalization—motivating ongoing work in adaptive teacher selection, data-free distillation, and task-aware compression design.

papers_seen.author: Holt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central Utility, Practical Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into compact student models so that high-performing systems can run under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, features, attention, relations) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to produce deployable models. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on task-aware choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and explicit handling of bias, low-frequency behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Approaches vary by what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel statistics, or decision-boundary information), by whether original training data are available, and by whether the goal is efficiency, robustness, privacy, or domain adaptation. Empirical work across vision, multimodal, speech, and natural language tasks shows that careful choices of transfer targets, loss formulations, teacher ensembles, and training schedules can yield compact models that approach — and in some cases match or exceed — teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties that prevent perfect belief matching, distribution-shift and heterogeneity issues in federated or data-free settings, and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When applied with attention to the task, available data, and student capacity, KD can deliver substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving most of the teacher's performance. Success depends on selecting what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align teacher and student (layer mapping, projectors, annealing), and how to handle limited or private data (data-free synthesis, adversarial generators, teacher-free regularizers). Although KD is broadly effective, it is not a panacea: failures arise from teacher-student mismatch, domain shift, optimization issues, and transferred biases, motivating targeted protocols and continued research into privacy-aware, robust, and automated distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for compressing large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings shows KD frequently recovers much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of broader compression pipelines and adopts safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable component of a compression pipeline and adapted to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: it must be combined with projector or layer-mapping techniques, ensemble and adversarial strategies where appropriate, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) while explicitly mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer, low-frequency degradation, and data scarcity. Continued theoretical and empirical work is needed to standardize best practices, automate signal selection, and robustly distill structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible, but Not Panacea Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students and for transferring task- or modality-specific capabilities. KD supports many transfer targets and training protocols and can be combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. However, reliable outcomes require careful teacher–student design, attention to data and privacy constraints, and targeted solutions for failure modes such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and preserved low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Methods vary by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), by how teachers and students are arranged (offline, online, ensemble, self-distillation), and by how distillation is integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free regimes). KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can improve robustness or generalization in some settings, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful handling of bias, distribution shift, and privacy considerations.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — A Position and Recommended Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows that KD can reduce inference cost, latency, and memory requirements and enable deployment under privacy, communication, and resource constraints. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, unbiased, or optimal compressed models: failures arise from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, transfer of teacher errors and biases, poor handling of low-frequency phenomena, and vulnerability under distribution shift or adversarial attack. Practical compression therefore treats KD as a core component within an integrated pipeline—combining representation-aware objectives, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, adversarial or synthetic-data generation for data-scarce regimes, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to realize reliable, resource-aware students.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical framework for producing compact models from larger teachers. When designed with attention to what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary compression techniques to apply, KD reliably yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss across modalities and tasks. However, KD is context-dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful treatment of bias, low-frequency phenomena, and domain shift. Best practice treats KD as a central component of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, a diverse toolbox of distillation targets, training protocols, and data strategies has been developed. Practical deployment typically treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) while attending to data regimes, teacher–student alignment, and risks such as transferred bias and degraded behavior on rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically indispensable technique for compressing and adapting large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD is highly versatile—supporting logits-, feature-, attention- and relation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and privacy- or data-constrained workflows—but it is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, what signals are transferred, data availability and distribution, and careful training protocol design. Treating KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines and combining it with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, data augmentation, and curriculum strategies) leads to the most reliable deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or specialized teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed many variants—logit transfer, feature- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives, ensemble- and teacher-aware algorithms, data-free and few-shot protocols, and meta-learned teachers—to address practical deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, device heterogeneity) while also pursuing robustness, fairness, and task adaptation. This synthesis summarizes dominant methods, representative applications, empirical patterns, and common failure modes that guide practical use and future research.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students that preserves much of teacher functionality while reducing latency, memory, and compute. KD methods span soft-logit matching, intermediate-representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD delivers substantial practical benefits across modalities and tasks when applied as part of a task-aware compression pipeline, but it is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a versatile, task-aware toolkit that enables compact, efficient, and deployable models across modalities. KD methods—ranging from logit-based soft targets to feature-, layer-, and relation-level matching, and including self-, multi-teacher, data-free, and online variants—consistently trade small accuracy loss for large gains in latency, memory, and privacy. Reliable application requires careful attention to teacher quality and compatibility, what to transfer, the data regime, and interactions with regularizers and complementary compression methods. When designed around deployment constraints and task objectives, KD delivers practical, often substantial improvements for on-device inference, domain adaptation, federated settings, and robustness-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. KD methods vary by what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structure), how teachers and students are paired (single, ensemble, multi-teacher, or self-distillation), and by constraints on data, privacy, and deployment hardware. Across vision, language, speech, graphs, and reinforcement learning, KD produces compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, lower memory, and operation under communication- or privacy-constrained settings. However, gains depend on teacher quality, data used for distillation, and architectural alignment; practical pipelines therefore combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design choices to close optimization and generalization gaps.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Necessity, Limits, and a Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling reduced memory, lower-latency inference, and new capabilities such as task-adaptive compression, multi-task transfer, and interpretable surrogates. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, dataset and distribution mismatches, teacher bias transfer, and design choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational structure) strongly affect outcomes. The most reliable results come from combining KD with complementary techniques (teacher adaptation, selective or curriculum-driven sample selection, representation matching, low-precision numerics, and scaled training procedures) and from tailoring the procedure to task- and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and communication while often preserving—and sometimes improving—task performance. A broad family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive signals) and protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co-distillation, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free/zero-shot) has been developed and combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and neural architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. The effectiveness of KD depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and nature of data (real or synthetic), and design choices about what and how to transfer; common failure modes include teacher error propagation, teacher–student mismatch, optimization gaps, and degraded modeling of rare phenomena. Best practice is to treat KD as a toolkit—selecting signals, mappings, and curricula appropriate to the task and constraints and combining KD with other compression strategies and safeguards for privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, compute, or privacy. Methods range from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and specialized data strategies. KD has enabled strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks (classification, generation, translation, graph learning, and recommender systems) but requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors. Key practical themes include selecting appropriate distillation signals, handling teacher–student capacity and architecture mismatches, designing or synthesizing data when originals are unavailable, and integrating KD with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Modalities, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high-performing deep learning models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. A broad set of distillation strategies—ranging from soft-label supervision and feature mimicking to data-free (zero-shot) distillation, adversarially guided feature transfer, self-distillation, and automated architecture search guided by teacher models—enable substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while preserving or even improving performance across vision, language, multimodal, and sequence tasks. Best practice combines input-side methods (data augmentation and mixup), representation-level transfer, and careful teacher-student design choices to match the deployment objectives (efficiency, fairness, interpretability, or privacy).

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—from soft-target (logit) transfer to feature- and relational-level objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and task-aware adaptations—has been developed and applied across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and objective design are aligned; persistent challenges include data scarcity, teacher–student architecture mismatch, transferred biases, and reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Findings from the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. The literature treats KD as a flexible, configurable component of compression pipelines rather than a single recipe: methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel- or relation-level signals), how transfer is organized (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free/zero-shot), and how KD is combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, adversarial training). Empirical evidence shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the chosen distillation signals and objectives, and data availability or synthesis strategies. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable, task-aware tool integrated with other compression and robustness practices.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, often ensemble or pre-trained, teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD includes matching teacher outputs (soft logits), imitating intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structures, and using multi-teacher, online, self-, or data-free protocols. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. While KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve student generalization, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and match, and careful choice of distillation signals; persistent challenges include optimization gaps, distribution shift, low-frequency/rare-case degradation, bias transfer, and federated or heterogeneous-device constraints. Ongoing work focuses on principled objectives, layer-mapping strategies, privacy- and data-aware distillation, and robust, task-aware pipelines for production deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to reduce the resource footprint of large neural networks while preserving performance. The literature surveys a range of approaches — from vanilla teacher-student soft-target transfers to layer-wise, attention- and channel-wise methods, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with pruning and adversarial training — and demonstrates successful applications across NLP, speech, vision, graph, and multimodal problems. Empirical results show effective speedups and parameter reductions with modest accuracy loss; theoretical and empirical analyses also connect KD to label-smoothing and regularization effects that can improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Non-Automatic Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when practitioners treat it as a configurable set of techniques—logit supervision, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial or contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online co-training, and data-free synthesis—combined with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful choices about teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and safeguards for robustness and privacy. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on explicit design choices and remains constrained by issues such as data scarcity, domain shift, teacher biases, optimization mismatch, and fidelity on low-frequency phenomena. The most reliable outcomes come from integrated pipelines that mix signal types, adapt teachers to students, and evaluate across deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD has been adapted into many variants and protocols and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods to produce deployable models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The technique yields substantial practical gains across modalities and tasks when teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and alignment of objectives are addressed; nevertheless, KD has well-documented failure modes and open challenges that require careful engineering and further research.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool: Integrating Distillation with Representation, Data, and Architecture Strategies for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, more deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone is rarely sufficient to meet real-world deployment constraints: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention), and access to or synthesis of suitable training data. Best results arise when KD is embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level matching, projector or layer-mapping modules, data and curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Careful attention to optimization, robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors is required to avoid propagating teacher errors and to produce reliable compact models for downstream applications.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster students to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and compute. A diverse set of distillation targets and training paradigms—soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate feature and attention-map imitation, layer-wise mapping, adversarial and data-free generation of surrogate examples, online and multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, and integration with architecture search or pruning—have been developed and adapted to vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of the teacher's accuracy (and in some settings improves generalization or robustness) when combined with task-aware choices of signals to transfer, data augmentation, and teacher-student design; remaining gaps and failure modes are linked to teacher quality, data availability and distribution shift, heterogeneous architectures, and fairness or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. KD encompasses logits-based, feature- and representation-level, multi-teacher, online, self-distillation, and privacy-aware variants, and its effectiveness depends on choosing what to transfer, matching student capacity to teacher signals, and integrating complementary compression and training practices. When combined with architecture-aware design, augmentation or synthetic-data generation, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols, KD enables deployable models across resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. The literature shows a broad family of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), multiple training paradigms (offline, online, co-distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free), and frequent combination with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD works both as a method for transferring predictive behavior and as an implicit regularizer, but its empirical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability (including synthesized or data‑free regimes), and careful engineering choices to mitigate optimization gaps, distributional mismatch, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, KD techniques (logits, feature/attention matching, relational objectives, adversarial and data‑free protocols, and ensemble/online schemes) often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when paired with appropriate data strategies, pretraining, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD has concrete limits — teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, rare‑token degradation, and failures under distribution shift or scarce/private data — which motivate task‑aware design, multi‑signal objectives, and integration with other compression primitives. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, domain examples, practical guidelines, and open challenges documented in the selected literature.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more socially or operationally suitable models. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks KD has been shown to preserve much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on constrained hardware and in privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. KD is most effective when combined with complementary practices such as pre-training, data augmentation, careful layer-matching, ensemble guidance, and hardware-aware pruning.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD variants—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and using data-free or adversarial generation—enable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical and analytical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance, sometimes improve generalization, and enable deployment under privacy or resource constraints, while remaining sensitive to teacher quality, data availability, and teacher–student alignment.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. When combined with architecture-aware design, layer- and feature-level objectives, adversarial or relational losses, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, NAS), KD enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss and can sometimes improve generalization. KD also faces clear limits—teacher bias, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and optimization instability—that require task-aware curricula, multi-teacher or ensemble strategies, and careful selection of distilled signals. This paper argues that KD should be the first-line instrument in compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP, provided practitioners adopt principled protocols that address known failure modes and integrate KD with complementary methods for the target deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring capabilities of large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of their task performance. Approaches span matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mappings, attention- and projector-based transfers, data-free and zero-shot schemes, multi-teacher and online protocols, and integrations with quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical work across language, vision, 3D perception, retrieval, and federated settings shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation is combined with suitable data strategies, teacher design, and complementary compression methods. Important open challenges remain in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive regimes, robust transfer across heterogeneous architectures, and principled selection of what and how to transfer.
