papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Bounded for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD provides flexible transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), supports data-limited and privacy-sensitive regimes via synthetic- or generator-based approaches, and interoperates with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency and memory constraints. Nevertheless, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data and capacity matching, and explicit mitigation of bias and distribution-shift risks, so it should be used as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from larger or auxiliary teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Its practical value is greatest when integrated with complementary compression primitives and when adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. However, KD also has clear limits—teacher–student capacity gaps, data scarcity or mismatch, and transferred biases or robustness failures—that require targeted mitigation and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Limitations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible method for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models across vision, language, speech, and recommendation systems. KD works both as a stand-alone compression technique and as a complementary tool that combines well with pruning, quantization, multi-teacher strategies, and privacy-aware or federated settings. While highly effective in practice, KD has limits—especially around data availability, heterogeneity, and theoretical understanding—that recent work addresses with data-free methods, meta-learning teachers, and principled analyses.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and deployment-ready students while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation techniques include matching logits (soft labels), feature- and layer-level imitation, ensemble and online schemes, data-free approaches, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Practical success depends on teacher quality and design, how and what information is transferred, availability and nature of data used for distillation, and how distillation is integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications span NLP (BERT compression, reading comprehension, language generation), vision and generative models (GANs, lipreading, 3D detection), recommender systems, and graphs. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher-student architectures, preserving fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, preventing transfer of teacher biases, and robust distillation under distribution shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models. KD succeeds most reliably when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline: practitioners should select appropriate transfer targets (logits, features, attention, relational signals), adapt objectives to student capacity and data regime, and combine distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies). While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities, it is not a universal cure—limitations such as teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and the risk of propagating biases require targeted mitigations and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool for Compression, Robustness, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into efficient students while also serving as a lever for regularization, robustness, privacy, fairness, interpretability, and continual/multi-task learning. When applied thoughtfully—combining soft-label distillation with feature- and representation-level matching, layer mapping, attention or projector modules, and task-aware curricula—KD can produce lightweight models that approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance on constrained devices and specialized tasks. However, KD is not automatic: optimization difficulties, data heterogeneity, and mismatches in the information transferred (e.g., for low-frequency tokens or internal features) limit its effectiveness unless complemented by targeted methodological choices. I argue that KD should be treated as a principled toolbox rather than a single recipe: choose distillation targets (outputs, features, internal representations), mapping strategies (many-to-many layer mapping, attention, projectors), and auxiliary safeguards (privacy-preserving noise, fairness interventions, adversarial distillation) to align compression goals with safety and utility requirements.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods span soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-representation and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free protocols, and task-aware layer mapping and projector modules. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and mitigation of transferred biases and robustness deficits.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been adapted across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) to produce smaller, faster, or more robust models while attempting to retain performance of larger teachers. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational information, or structural/topological properties), how transfer is scheduled or weighted (confidence-aware, progressive replacement, or multi-teacher aggregation), and how distillation is combined with other compression methods (pruning, architecture search, or compact operator substitution). Empirical work shows strong practical benefits—improved runtime, memory, and sometimes robustness or fairness—while theoretical and analytical work begins to explain when and why distillation helps (e.g., role of soft targets, label smoothing analogies, and behavior with imperfect teachers). Remaining challenges include transferring rare-word or low-frequency information in sequence tasks, preserving relational/global structure in graph and link tasks, adapting to evolving domains, and automating generator compression for GANs. This synthesis summarizes key methods, insights, and open directions from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of KD objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation, data‑free and adversarial approaches, and projector or curriculum-based engineering—has been developed and applied across vision and language tasks. Distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints but is not universally guaranteed: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of transfer signals and training procedures. The practical consensus is to treat KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool that Requires Task-Aware, Complementary Engineering
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for producing compact models from large teachers that supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints and student capacity. Best outcomes arise when KD is treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes representation alignment, data- and task-aware strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. A rich set of methods—ranging from logits/soft-target supervision to intermediate-feature matching, contrastive and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants—has been developed and is routinely combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture/parameter adaptations). Empirical and conceptual work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, signal choice, data availability or synthesis strategy, and careful integration with other compression tools. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable component of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central Benefits, Practical Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD enables deployment under resource, privacy, and latency constraints, and can be adapted for task-specific compression, federated and data-free settings, low-precision inference, and bias- or domain-aware transfer. However, KD also carries practical limits: optimization gaps that prevent perfect teacher matching, transfer of teacher biases, failures on low-frequency phenomena, and sensitivity to data availability and teacher-student compatibility. To realize KD's promise practitioners should choose what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), consider multi-teacher and confidence-weighting schemes, leverage task-aware architecture search when appropriate, and adopt specialized strategies (data-free generation, reverse distillation, counterfactual augmentation, or federated protocols) to address specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational constraints) and can operate in offline, online, data‑free, and federated regimes. Its empirical strengths span vision, language, speech, multimodal, and distributed training settings. However, KD is not a standalone panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals and data strategy, and explicit steps to mitigate transferred biases, low‑frequency failures, and distribution shift. The most reliable compression outcomes treat KD as the practical core of a task‑aware pipeline that integrates representation matching, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the behavior and performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when integrated thoughtfully into compression pipelines and paired with complementary techniques, but its effectiveness is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student design, data strategy, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained student models so they retain functionality while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logits-based soft-label supervision to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware mappings, adversarial and contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or heterogeneous-device protocols. Empirical and theoretical work indicates KD often acts both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, task alignment, and careful design of objectives and model interfaces. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data scarcity or domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, principled layer-to-layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating teacher-induced biases.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques that transfers behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and model size while often preserving most of the original performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline—choosing appropriate transfer targets, adapting objectives to student capacity and data regimes, and combining distillation with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. However, KD is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections (including bias), data scarcity or privacy constraints, and difficulty preserving rare or structured behaviors require targeted mitigations, careful evaluation, and continued methodological and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Sawyer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models. KD variants include matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention, relational and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture/architecture-search, and data strategies), KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, outcomes are context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and training design materially shape success. Practical use treats KD as a configurable component within integrated compression pipelines rather than a turnkey algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models. KD routinely yields large efficiency gains (reduced memory, compute, and latency) while preserving much of teacher performance when applied with task‑aware objectives, appropriate teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including privacy or data‑free regimes), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and degraded handling of rare phenomena. Treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with targeted algorithmic and engineering practices, KD enables practical, deployable compression across modalities and settings.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. A wide range of distillation targets and protocols has been developed, and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design. While distilled students often recover much of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, important limitations and open problems remain—particularly around data scarcity, distribution shift, bias transfer, and principled selection of distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Component — Advocating Task‑Aware, Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Empirical evidence across modalities shows KD routinely reduces latency, memory, and compute while preserving task performance when combined with appropriate design choices. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, hardware-optimal efficiency, or reliable performance under data scarcity and distribution shift; it must be integrated into a task-aware compression pipeline that includes teacher–student co‑design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving or sometimes improving task performance. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component and combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, layer mapping, or data synthesis), KD yields favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities and supports deployment under latency, privacy, and data-constraint requirements. However, realizing KD's benefits reliably requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, what signals are transferred, how layers are aligned, and which training data or augmentations are used.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD operates via soft-label (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial or generative synthesis of data, and many hybrid protocols. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to task- and data-specific constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and careful objective design. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a central, configurable component of an integrated compression strategy rather than a one-shot solution.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broadly applicable framework that enables compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teachers to smaller students. KD methods span logits, intermediate-feature and relational matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and cross-modal variants, and complementary integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance and provides regularization benefits, its practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one-shot cure, and addresses robustness, privacy, and distribution-shift concerns through protocol design and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. KD has been extended from soft-label/logit transfer to a rich set of representation- and task-level objectives (feature matching, attention and relation alignment, projector modules, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data-free methods). When applied with task awareness — choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, privacy, and hardware constraints — KD consistently enables substantial reductions in size and latency with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and low-frequency behaviors. Best practice treats KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, and hardware-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable technique for compressing and adapting large neural models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across computer vision, generative modeling, cross-modal systems, and NLP, distillation can be combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, adversarial training, and feature alignment) to meet deployment constraints and domain requirements. Success depends on teacher design, the availability and nature of data used for transfer, careful alignment of representations, and training objectives that address optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or more expressive models (teachers) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods extend beyond simple teacher-logit matching to include feature and representation alignment, relational objectives, contrastive methods, adversarial or boundary-focused sampling, curriculum and progressive replacement schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware workflows. KD has been successfully applied across vision, language, speech, graph-structured data, retrieval, and constrained-device deployments, and is commonly combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency and memory budgets. Key practical concerns include what to transfer, how to cope with teacher-student mismatch and limited or private data, optimization barriers that prevent perfect mimicry, and measurement of distilled model robustness and fairness. While empirical progress has been large and diverse, theoretical and systems-level problems remain active areas of research.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques that make large, high-performing models practical for deployment by transferring behavior, representations, or decision structure to smaller models. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when combined with appropriate supervision signals, data practices, and architectural alignment, but it also has important failure modes—propagated teacher errors, sensitivity to data distribution and teacher quality, and limits when student capacity is insufficient. I argue KD should be treated as a foundational component of model-compression pipelines, applied thoughtfully and in combination with complementary methods (augmentation, pruning/quantization, privacy mechanisms, and federated protocols) to realize robust, efficient systems for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable collection of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary models (“teachers”) into smaller, more deployable models (“students”). Over the last decade KD has diversified beyond simple soft-label matching to include feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data‑free protocols, and online or self-distillation schemes. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers much of a teacher’s performance while enabling reductions in parameters, latency, and memory, but reliable deployment requires task‑aware design, careful handling of data and teacher imperfections, and integration with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to reduce the resource footprint of large neural networks while preserving performance. The literature surveys a range of approaches — from vanilla teacher-student soft-target transfers to layer-wise, attention- and channel-wise methods, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with pruning and adversarial training — and demonstrates successful applications across NLP, speech, vision, graph, and multimodal problems. Empirical results show effective speedups and parameter reductions with modest accuracy loss; theoretical and empirical analyses also connect KD to label-smoothing and regularization effects that can improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure, and decision-boundary or synthetic-data signals), training protocols (single/multi-teacher, online/self-distillation, task- and layer-aware schedules), and architecture-aware adaptations (projectors, layer mapping, and combinations with pruning/quantization/NAS) has been developed. Empirically, properly designed distillation pipelines recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, and can be combined with complementary compression methods to meet device and domain requirements. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps, teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift and data scarcity (including privacy- and data-free regimes), and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single algorithm, KD enables large reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on task-aware choices—what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, how to generate or select transfer data, and which complementary compression techniques to combine. KD also has clear failure modes (data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena) that require targeted remedies. With appropriate safeguards and joint optimization with pruning, quantization, or architecture search, KD should be a primary method in compression pipelines, applied conditionally and validated for the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Poole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques provide a practical toolkit for shrinking large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their task performance. Over the last decade researchers have developed a range of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational maps, contrastive signals), teacher-student schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, lifelong), and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search, block-structured pruning). Empirical work shows KD often acts both as information transfer and regularization, enabling deployment across vision, language, multimodal, graph, generative, and medical-imaging tasks; however, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of propagated errors or biases. Best practice is task- and capacity-aware design that combines appropriate distilled signals, alignment of inputs/representations, and complementary compression methods to meet target constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Summers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while retaining much of task performance. Modern KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis. KD is commonly combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence indicates KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and suitable data strategies are aligned, but its success is context-dependent and requires task-aware design to mitigate limits related to teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled Toolbox for Practical and Responsible Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolbox that can produce compact, deployable models when combined with complementary design choices. Properly applied—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to map layers, and which auxiliary techniques to use (pretraining, curriculum, adversarial or privacy safeguards)—KD can deliver students that approach or sometimes match teacher performance while enabling latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployment. At the same time, KD has clear failure modes (data heterogeneity, low-frequency phenomena, imperfect teachers, and optimization challenges) that demand targeted mitigations rather than blind application.

papers_seen.author: Spence
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques that should be treated as an essential, task-aware component of model-compression pipelines rather than a one-size-fits-all solution. Properly designed KD—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, selecting or synthesizing suitable data, and integrating complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—regularly yields compact models that preserve most teacher performance for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. However, KD has predictable failure modes (teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and degradation on rare outputs) that require explicit mitigation and evaluation in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods include transferring soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals, and can be applied in offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free settings. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables many practical applications across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, available data (or synthesis strategies), and careful objective design. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and targeted data strategies—and adopt safeguards for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining substantial parts of teacher performance. A broad family of distillation targets and training protocols has been developed (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive signals; offline, online, self-, multi-teacher, and data-free variants). Practical success depends on aligning the distillation signal to task and student capacity and on combining distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Key challenges include teacher–student capacity and architecture mismatch, limited or unavailable data, propagation of teacher biases or errors, distribution shift, and difficulties preserving low-frequency or structured behaviors. Continued progress requires principled choices about what, when, and how to transfer knowledge, better theory linking distillation choices to student generalization, and engineering pipelines that pair KD with task-aware data and model design.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practical Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when combined with deployment-aware design choices and complementary compression tools. However, realizing robust, fair, and privacy-preserving compressed models requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and method selection.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted strategy for producing smaller, faster, or more interpretable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact student models. A wide range of techniques has been developed that go beyond matching final outputs to include intermediate representation matching, attention/feature imitation, contrastive and relational objectives, and architecture-aware optimization; KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and reinforcement learning demonstrates that careful selection of teacher signals, student capacity, data regimes, and auxiliary compression methods strongly affects final trade-offs between efficiency and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and properties of larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and privacy-sensitive settings, KD variants transfer logits, intermediate representations, relations, or synthesized data to produce students that meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often yields favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and model size, but its success depends on data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and careful objective and training choices.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied set of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teacher ensembles or single models. The literature shows a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (soft logits, feature- and attention-level targets, relational/contrastive objectives), protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, self- or co-distillation), and engineering integrations (projector adapters, curriculum or confidence-weighting, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and cross-modal tasks indicates that carefully designed KD pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and mitigating failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare-output behavior, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely used family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature develops multi-level transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), multi‑teacher and online variants, data-aware and data‑free protocols, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks when teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and mapping between teacher and student are carefully managed; however, success is context-dependent and limited by optimization gaps, data scarcity, capacity mismatch, and the risk of transferring teacher artifacts or biases. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable component of broader compression workflows tailored to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized models by transferring information from larger or alternative teachers into compact students. KD variants—ranging from logits and feature matching to relational, contrastive, and data-free protocols—have been demonstrated across vision, speech, and NLP to deliver favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. At the same time, KD’s success depends on teacher quality, signal choice, data regime, and careful training design, and it is most reliable when integrated with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware engineering. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, configurable element of any compression pipeline, but not as a standalone solution: use KD deliberately, combine it with other methods, and adopt practices that mitigate its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses the capabilities of large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A variety of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, channel statistics, relational signals, or synthesized data) and protocols (offline teacher, online co-training, self-distillation, meta-learned teachers, teacher-free schemes, and data-free variants) have been developed to address deployment constraints across vision, language, speech, retrieval, detection, and generative tasks. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation objectives and training schedules often preserve most teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but important trade-offs remain — including transferred biases, optimization and capacity gaps, data access and privacy constraints, and difficulties under distribution shift — motivating numerous methodological refinements and open research directions.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance and functionality of larger teacher models. KD is highly versatile—operating at the level of logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and generative models). However, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and the design of distillation objectives; consequently KD should be treated as a configurable component that is combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and empirically supported family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational constraints, and many online or data-free protocols. While KD frequently enables large reductions in latency, memory, and compute with modest performance loss, its success is context dependent: it requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and task‑aware choices of distilled signals and complementary compression methods. When applied as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline — combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, careful data strategies, and safeguards against bias or distributional shift — KD is often the most practical and flexible first‑line approach for real-world model deployment.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for producing compact models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models. The approach spans simple soft-label transfer to richer objectives that match intermediate representations, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures, and supports many protocols (offline, online/co-distillation, multi-teacher, self-distillation and data-free variants). KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curriculum learning, and data strategies—and when choices about transfer targets, layer alignment, and data are tailored to task and deployment constraints.
